questions.label: Launch standard edition retail price (USD)

questions.label: Early access/demo pricing
questions.rationale: Free playable demo was available pre-launch without charge, granting +5 points for free demo availability.

questions.label: Microtransactions at launch
questions.rationale: No microtransactions were present at launch in 1998; contemporary PC market did not support MTX payment models. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Loot boxes/randomized paid rewards
questions.rationale: No loot boxes or randomized paid reward systems existed in Half-Life at launch. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Battle pass/subscription model
questions.rationale: No battle pass, subscription model, or recurring payment system at launch. Award +5 points.

questions.label: In-game advertisements
questions.rationale: No persistent in-game advertisements or ad screens observed. Baseline neutral score of 0 points.

questions.label: Post-launch support, updates, and DLCs
questions.rationale: Valve provided multi-year post-launch support including patches, expansions (Opposing Force, Blue Shift), and community updates throughout the 2000s. Award +10 points for 2+ years of continuous support.

questions.label: Announcement lead time before US launch
questions.rationale: Official announcement: June 1997 (E3 1997); US PC launch: November 19, 1998. Elapsed period: ~17.5 months, within the 18-month window. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Pre-launch trailers, content updates, community feedback
questions.rationale: Multiple pre-launch trailers and marketing materials were distributed. Free demo was published pre-launch responding to community demand. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Advertised features present at launch
questions.rationale: All major advertised systems, campaign storyline, and multiplayer modes were fully implemented and functional at initial launch. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Average expected duration of main campaign
questions.rationale: Half-Life main campaign delivers approximately 20-22 hours of core gameplay for first-time players. Award +5 points for >20 hour duration.

questions.label: Variety of outcomes/game endings
questions.rationale: Single primary campaign ending with limited branching. However, robust level design permits multiple tactical paths through maps. Award +3 points for single-ending campaign with solid map design.

questions.label: Accessibility features (subtitles, colorblind modes, difficulty adjustments)
questions.rationale: Subtitles and difficulty sliders present. No native colorblind mode, but core experience remains accessible. Award +2 points for comprehensive baseline options.

questions.label: Control input methods supported
questions.rationale: Keyboard & mouse natively supported with full rebinding. Controller support not standard in 1998 era. Award +2 points for primary input method support.

questions.label: Localization and translation breadth
questions.rationale: Half-Life was localized into multiple languages including German, French, Italian, Spanish, Japanese, and Korean. Award +6 points for 3+ language translations with localized subtitles.

questions.label: State of initial player reviews after first month of launch
questions.rationale: Half-Life achieved 'Positive' to 'Overwhelmingly Positive' community consensus post-launch. Metacritic averaged in the 90s, IGN and GameSpot both awarded high scores (9+/10). Award +5 points.

questions.label: Game completely playable offline
questions.rationale: Half-Life is fully playable offline without any remote authentication requirement, dead-server dependency, or mandatory online account linking. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Launch-day cross-platform multiplayer support
questions.rationale: Q18 Rule Path: single_player_exemption_applied. Half-Life is primarily single-player in core design (campaign is solo-focused). Multiplayer component is optional and secondary. Single-player exemption applies; award +10 points automatically.

questions.label: Modding support level
questions.rationale: Valve shipped Half-Life with comprehensive modding tools and SDK. Community modding thrived (Counter-Strike, Team Fortress, etc.). Award +5 points for full, open modding support.

questions.label: File size optimization
questions.rationale: Half-Life install footprint (~1.4 GB after expansions) was well-optimized relative to comparable FPS titles of 1998-2000 era. Award +5 points for average or below file size.

questions.label: Launch standard edition retail price (USD)
questions.rationale: Prey (2006) launched at standard PC retail ~$49.99 USD. Consistent pricing tier with contemporary AAA FPS games. No premium edition differentiation. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Early access/demo pricing
questions.rationale: Prey had public demos available pre-launch without tiered pricing or early access gate (industry standard 2006). Unrestricted public demo access. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Microtransactions at launch
questions.rationale: Zero microtransactions at launch. Single-purchase business model with complete content access. Multiplayer modes added via free patches post-launch (not monetized). Award +5 points.

questions.label: Loot boxes/randomized paid rewards
questions.rationale: No loot boxes, gacha mechanics, or randomized paid rewards. Single-player campaign has no randomization beyond standard FPS enemy spawns. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Battle pass/subscription model
questions.rationale: No battle pass, seasonal content model, or subscription requirement. All multiplayer patches and content additions distributed free to game owners. Award +5 points.

questions.label: In-game advertisements
questions.rationale: No in-game advertisements, billboards, or product placement observed. Game is completely ad-free. Neutral baseline score of 0 points.

questions.label: Post-launch support, updates, and DLCs
questions.rationale: Substantial post-launch support documented. Launch was stable with only minor bugs. Patches released through 2007 including multiplayer implementation via free patches (deathmatch, team deathmatch modes). No story DLC or pay-locked content. Award +5 points for 1+ year active support.

questions.label: Announcement lead time before US launch
questions.rationale: Game announced at E3 1997 (industry showcase). US launch July 11, 2006. Elapsed period ~17 months from announcement window. Within +5 threshold (announced within 18 months per V1.06). Award +5 points.

questions.label: Pre-launch trailers, content updates, community feedback
questions.rationale: Strong marketing campaign across development. Official trailers released throughout development cycle. Community engagement via forums, conference demos, and preview events. Player feedback loop evident in patch development. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Advertised features present at launch
questions.rationale: All advertised features delivered at launch. Gravity mechanic (primary marketing hook) fully functional and integrated throughout campaign. Story, boss encounters, character progression all as advertised. Multiplayer marked as 'to follow' (met expectation). Award +5 points.

questions.label: Average expected duration of main campaign
questions.rationale: Single-player campaign documented at 12-15 hours for average playthrough across all agent sources. Multiple difficulty levels (Easy/Normal/Hard) provide replay incentive. Meets full campaign duration threshold. Award +5 points for >10 hour campaign.

questions.label: Variety of outcomes/game endings
questions.rationale: Single canonical ending to narrative (linear story arc). Outcome variety exists through difficulty levels affecting challenge/pacing, hidden areas and exploration paths, weapon load-out choices affecting combat approach, and optional collectibles/achievements. Not multiple endings, but meaningful internal branching. Award +3 points.

questions.label: Accessibility features (subtitles, colorblind modes, difficulty adjustments)
questions.rationale: Prey (2006) provided difficulty sliders (Easy/Normal/Hard), full voice acting with subtitle support for hearing accessibility, and tutorial levels. No dedicated colorblind mode. Released 2006 (no legacy exemption). Constrained by 2006 technical standards, not design negligence. Award +2 points.

questions.label: Control input methods supported
questions.rationale: Launched with keyboard/mouse support standard to FPS genre (optimal for 2006 PC gaming). Gamepad support added post-launch via patches. Released 2006 (no legacy exemption for Q14—only pre-2000 releases force +2). Single primary input family at launch. Award +2 points.

questions.label: Localization and translation breadth
questions.rationale: Prey (2006) commercially distributed internationally with multi-language support. Evidence: Strong international marketing, European releases confirmed (Eurogamer 2006 coverage), standard AAA localization practices for $50 publisher title. Estimated: English, German, French, Italian, Spanish at minimum. Award +5 points for 3+ language translations.

questions.label: State of initial player reviews after first month of launch
questions.rationale: Metacritic score 79 (Generally Favorable Reviews). User score 7.5 (Mixed but positive). Critical consensus strong: IGN 8.0/10, GameSpot 8.0/10, EuroGamer 8/10, 1UP A grade, PC Zone 86%. Review aggregate demonstrates critical success at launch. User complaints (difficulty spikes, AI allies) minor relative to positive reception. Award +5 points.

questions.label: Game completely playable offline
questions.rationale: Full offline playability confirmed across all research sources. Single-player campaign requires NO online authentication, NO server connectivity, NO account login. SecuROM DRM was local-check only (not online-verified). Multiplayer servers now offline but irrelevant to core game. Award +5 points for fully offline core experience.

questions.label: Launch-day cross-platform multiplayer support
questions.rationale: Q18 Rule Path: legacy_release_exemption_applied + single_player_exemption_applied. Prey (2006) released before 2010 cutoff, triggering legacy release exemption (Q18 → +10 before crossplay evaluation). Additionally, game is primarily single-player in design (campaign focus). Multiplayer added post-launch via patches (not launch feature). Per V1.06: apply single_player_exemption_applied and force Q18 to +10. Award +10 points.

questions.label: Modding support level
questions.rationale: Built on Unreal Engine 2 (mod-capable engine by design). However, no official mod tools, editor, or modding kit released by developers. Community developed small mods and tweaks (documented in guides), but limited scope compared to Half-Life 2 or Doom 3 (contemporaries with robust official support). Unofficial modding possible but not encouraged by developer. Award +2 points.

questions.label: File size optimization
questions.rationale: Install size 8 GB documented across all sources. For 2006 standards, this was substantial but reasonable (modern game distribution on 3 CDs = ~2.6 GB per disk). By 2006 era context, 8 GB shows competent optimization relative to peers (Half-Life 2 2004 was ~11 GB). Not exceptional efficiency, but well-balanced for era. Award +3 points.
